discussion_comments.comment_body: Should we add a code path here to use https://nodejs.org/api/buffer.html#blobstream when supported? Not sure how usable that is, but seems Node.js is adding the ability to make a Blob from a file which could be huge.

For any Node.js version where `require('stream/web')` doesn't work, this is going to cause a sync walk of the file system every time, since a `require()` failure is not added to the module cache like a success is. This would ideally be moved to only happen on the loading of this module, not on every single response write.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Gotcha. I guess I got confused because the benchmark is about different URLs, rather than the different options of the `query` middleware itself. For example, I think it would be more useful to test the 4 different query options we provide out of the box to each other, rather than testing urls to feed to just a single option (qs).
I suggest that we use for loop to avoid the performance penalty of closures. See http://jsperf.com/array-foreach-vs-for-loop.

Yes, it could be.

I explained why I put out try..catch block there, it's for performance reasons only, see PR description. If a certain string is correct, it would parse faster.

I did some benchmarks, and I got 2000 ms for N iterations of querystring.parse. Compare that to native speed 400 ms of decodeURIComponent. However, if URI is malformed, the entire try..catch block would take up 13000 ms, so it's kinda tradeoff.

I don't mind replacing, and it would simplify things. I just looked at node core and thought they did the right thing, and I don't have a personal opinion here.
